questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following are features of umbilical hernia in adults? 1. Patients are commonly overweight with a thinned and attenuated midline raphe. 2. Most patients complain of pain due to tissue tension. 3. Men are affected more commonly than women. 4. Hernia repair can be done by the technique described by Mayo. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 2 and 4

Adult umbilical hernia is an acquired hernia resulting from weakness of the umbilical ring due to raised intra-abdominal pressure and attenuation of the linea alba. It is commonly seen in obese individuals and multiparous women and usually requires mesh repair because of a high recurrence rate with simple suture repair.

Why is B correct?

• 1. Patients are commonly overweight with a thinned and attenuated midline raphe. ✅

• Obesity causes stretching and weakening of the linea alba, predisposing to umbilical hernia.

• 2. Most patients complain of pain due to tissue tension. ✅

• Adults commonly present with pain or discomfort, especially during coughing or exertion, due to tension on the hernia defect.

• 3. Men are affected more commonly than women. ❌

• Adult umbilical hernias are more common in women, particularly multiparous and obese women.

• 4. Hernia repair can be done by the technique described by Mayo. ✅

• Mayo’s repair (double-breasting technique) is the classic tissue repair for umbilical hernia, although mesh repair is preferred today for larger defects due to lower recurrence.
questions.learning: 1, 2 and 4 Adult umbilical hernia is an acquired hernia resulting from weakness of the umbilical ring due to raised intra-abdominal pressure and attenuation of the linea alba.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A 25-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department after a road traffic accident, presenting with bradycardia, elevated blood pressure, and a GCS score < 8. What is the most critical immediate step in managing this patient?
questions.explanation: In any trauma patient with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of less than 8 ("GCS 8, Intubate"), the most critical immediate step is securing a definitive airway through endotracheal intubation and providing mechanical ventilation (IPPV). This is mandatory to prevent hypoxia and hypercapnia, both of which cause cerebral vasodilation and exacerbate secondary brain injury. The patient’s bradycardia and hypertension (part of Cushing's triad) are ominous signs of severely increased intracranial pressure and impending brain herniation. While an urgent CT head (Option A) is essential for diagnosis, it should never be performed before the airway is secured and the patient is stabilized. Options C and D refer to suture materials and are entirely irrelevant to emergency neuro-trauma management. Stabilization focuses on "Airway, Breathing, and Circulation" (the ATLS ABCs). Following intubation, management shifts to neurosurgical consultation for potential evacuation of hematomas and monitoring of intracranial pressure. Rapid intervention is the key to minimizing permanent neurological damage
questions.learning: In any trauma patient with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of less than 8 ("GCS 8, Intubate"), the most critical immediate step is securing a definitive airway through endotracheal intubation and providing mechanical ventilation (IPPV).

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 32-year-old woman presents with intermenstrual bleeding after the insertion of an intrauterine device (IUD). She reports no other symptoms. What is the most appropriate initial management?
questions.explanation: Intermenstrual bleeding and spotting are the most common side effects associated with the insertion of an intrauterine device (IUD), particularly within the first three to six months of use. If the patient is clinically stable and reports no severe pain, fever, or heavy bleeding, the most appropriate initial step is to reassure her and observe. Most cases of IUD-related spotting resolve spontaneously as the uterine lining adapts to the device. Removing the IUD (Option A) is premature unless the bleeding is intolerable or persistent after several months. A pelvic ultrasound (Option C) is only indicated if there is suspicion of device displacement or other pelvic pathology. Prescribing hormonal therapy (Option D) is generally not the initial step for mild spotting immediately post-insertion. Patient education regarding the expected side-effect profile of the IUD is essential for improving long-term adherence and satisfaction with this effective contraceptive method
questions.learning: Intermenstrual bleeding and spotting are the most common side effects associated with the insertion of an intrauterine device (IUD), particularly within the first three to six months of use.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.text: A 30-year-old woman was brought to the psychiatric OPD by her friend. The patient claims that her boss is in love with her and stalks her. The woman’s friend refutes her claims. What is your diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Erotomania

Erotomania is a delusional disorder where the patient believes someone is in love with him/her, against evidence to the contrary. It is also known as De Clérambault syndrome.

The lover in the delusion is often a person of higher social status. It is more common in women.

Pearl PF1258: Types of delusions

THE TYPES OF DELUSIONS

Delusion of control

False belief that a person’s will, thoughts, or feelings are being controlled by external forces.

Delusion of grandeur or Megalomania

Exaggerated conception of one’s importance, power, or identity.

Delusion of infidelity or morbid jealousy or Othello syndrome

False belief that one’s lover is unfaithful. Sometimes called pathological jealousy.

Delusion of love or erotomania

False belief that another person is in love with them. In De Clerambault syndrome, the woman believes that a man, frequently older and of higher status, is in love with her.

Delusion of misidentification

Capgras syndrome: Belief that a familiar person has been replaced by an exact double i.e. an impostor.

Fregoli syndrome: Person holds a delusional belief that different people are in fact a single person who changes his or her appearance or is in disguise.

Nihilistic delusion

False belief that oneself, others or the world, is non-existent or about to end. When nihilistic delusion is accompanied by ideas concerning bodily function failure e.g. putrefaction of intestine etc, it is called Cotard syndrome.

Delusion of infestation

False belief that one is infested with small but visible organisms. As a monosymptomatic delusional disorder, this is called Ekbom syndrome.

Delusion of persecution

The most common delusion. False belief of being harassed or persecuted.

Delusion of poverty

The person strongly believes they are financially incapacitated.

Delusion of reference

False belief that the behavior of others has a particular and unusual significance, usually of a negative nature. The person may falsely feel that others are talking about them (e.g. the people on television are talking to or about the person).

Delusion of self-accusation

False feeling of remorse and guilt. Seen in depression with psychotic features.
questions.learning: Erotomania Erotomania is a delusional disorder where the patient believes someone is in love with him/her, against evidence to the contrary. It is also known as De Clérambault syndrome.

questions.subject: Ophthalmology
questions.text: A 72-year-old patient, known to have diabetes mellitus, presents with a gradual decrease in vision one month after undergoing cataract surgery. Fundoscopic examination reveals a characteristic honeycomb or flower-petal pattern in the retina. This finding is suggestive of which condition?
questions.explanation: The "honeycomb appearance" or "flower petal pattern" observed during fluorescein angiography of the retina is the classic finding for Cystoid Macular Edema (CME). This pattern results from the accumulation of fluid in cystic spaces within the Henle's layer of the macula. CME is a common cause of vision decrease following cataract surgery (Irvine-Gass syndrome), and the risk is significantly higher in patients with Diabetes Mellitus (DM). Central serous retinopathy (Option B) involves a localized serous detachment of the neurosensory retina, usually showing a "smoke-stack" leak on angiography. Retinal detachment (Option C) is a separation of the retina from the pigment epithelium. Diabetic retinopathy (Option D) encompasses a range of findings including microaneurysms and hemorrhages, but the specific petaloid appearance refers to the resulting macular edema. Management of post-surgical CME typically involves topical NSAIDs and corticosteroids. In diabetic patients, ensuring stable blood sugar levels is also critical for resolution
questions.learning: The "honeycomb appearance" or "flower petal pattern" observed during fluorescein angiography of the retina is the classic finding for Cystoid Macular Edema (CME).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: A muscle is attached to the area marked in the given image. What is the action of this muscle on the hip joint?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Extension and lateral rotation

The area marked in the given image is the gluteal tuberosity. The muscle that is inserted here is the gluteus maximus which causes extension and lateral rotation of the hip joint.

Gluteus maximus inserts onto iliotibial tract (3/4th part) and deep fibers (1/4th) attach on gluteal tuberosity (marked in image). It is supplied by the inferior gluteal nerve. It is the chief extensor of the lower limb at the hip joint. It additionally also causes lateral rotation, abduction.
questions.learning: Extension and lateral rotation — The area marked in the given image is the gluteal tuberosity. The muscle that is inserted here is the gluteus maximus which causes extension and lateral rotation of the hip joint.

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.text: A surgeon returns home from a party after many pegs of alcohol and was called to perform an emergency operation. During the operation, the assisting staff noticed the surgeon's hand shaking and instruments falling. He eventually nicks an artery and the patient collapses. Under which of the following terms will this incident be tried?
options: Civil negligence not amounting to criminal negligence
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Criminal negligence

The incident mentioned in the given scenario will be tried under criminal negligence.

Criminal negligence is when a doctor lacks a gross skill or care while treating, which results in serious injury/death of the patient, or when an illegal act is performed by a doctor or when an assaulted person dies. Most cases of criminal negligence occur due to drunkenness or usage of drugs, which leads to impaired efficiency.

Some of the examples are amputation of the wrong finger; leaving an instrument, tube, or sponge in the abdomen; incompetent administration of general anesthetic; and administrating the wrong substance in the eye, leading to visual loss.

The doctor is prosecuted by the police and charged in criminal court, when it is proved that no medical doctor in his ordinary senses would have done it. Contributory negligence cannot be used as a defense in criminal negligence.

Other options:

Option B: Civil negligence occurs as a result of lacking care and skill in the profession. Contributory negligence can be cited as a defense in civil negligence.

Option C: Therapeutic misadventure is a case that causes injury or death to the individual due to an unintentional act by a doctor or hospital. The physician is not liable for the injuries unless some negligence on his part contributed to the occurrence of the injury.

Option D: Dichotomy is a type of unethical act, wherein a physician offers or receives any gift or bonus for referring or procuring any patient for medical or surgical treatment.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A female patient presents to the outpatient department 10 days postpartum with a tender, fluctuant breast mass, high-grade fever, and cracked nipples. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The presence of a fluctuant mass in the breast, associated with fever and severe tenderness, is the classic clinical definition of a breast abscess. This typically occurs as a complication of untreated or inadequately treated acute mastitis (Option C). Mastitis itself involves inflammation, redness, and fever, but it does not yet have a localized collection of pus (fluctuance). Breast engorgement (Option A) occurs early in the postpartum period (Days 2–4) and involves bilateral, generalized swelling and discomfort, but not localized fluctuant masses or high-grade fever. Fibroadenoma (Option D) is a benign, painless, "mouse-in-the-breast" lump seen in younger women, unrelated to lactation or infection. The most common causative organism is Staphylococcus aureus, often entering through cracked nipples. Management of an abscess involves incision and drainage or needle aspiration, along with appropriate antibiotics and continued breast feeding or pumping from the affected side
questions.learning: The presence of a fluctuant mass in the breast, associated with fever and severe tenderness, is the classic clinical definition of a breast abscess. This typically occurs as a complication of untreated or inadequately treated acute mastitis (Option C).

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: An HIV patient presented with bouts of cough and fever. What is the selective medium used for investigation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Lowenstein-Jenson medium

A HIV patient with cough and fever is indicative of a tuberculosis infection. Lowenstein-Jenson medium is a selective medium used for Mycobacterium tuberculosis culture.

Lowenstein-Jenson medium is a selective medium used for the culture of Mycobacterium tuberculosis which causes tuberculosis. The presence of malachite green imparts a green colour and makes Lowenstein Jenson medium a selective media by inhibiting other bacteria.

Components of LJ medium:

* Egg: Provide fatty acids and protein required for the metabolism.

* Malachite green: Prevents growth of contaminants.

* Mineral salt solution: Buffer.

* Glycerol: Source of carbon, Favours growth of M. tuberculosis, but not M. bovis.

* L-asparagine: Source of Nitrogen.

Mycobacterium tuberculosis colonies on LJ medium are dry, rough, raised, and irregular with a wrinkled surface. They are creamy white or buff-colored, tenacious, and difficult to emulsify (rough, tough, buff).

Culture media used to cultivate Mycobacterium tuberculosis:

* Solid Culture Media: Lowenstein–Jensen: A commonly used, egg-based, selective media. contains malachite green, which prevents growth of other organisms.

* Liquid Culture Media: Middle Brook’s media: Used for preparation of antigens and vaccines, and sensitivity testing.

* Automated Culture Media: BACTEC 460: Uses radioisotopes, BacT alert: A colorimetric method, BACTEC MGIT: A fluorometric detection method.

Other options:

Option A: Thayer-Martin medium is used to isolate Neisseria gonorrhoeae because the antimicrobials present in it, suppress the growth of other commensal organisms which may inhibit the growth of N.gonorrhoeae. Thayer Martin Medium selectively favors the growth of Neisseria by inhibiting the growth of gram-positive organisms with Vancomycin, gram-negative organisms (except Neisseria) with Trimethoprim and Colistin, and fungi with Nystatin

Thayer-Martin medium contains antimicrobials like vancomycin 3.0 mg, colistin 7.5 mg, and nystatin 12.5 units per ml of agar, in chocolate agar.

Option C:  MacConkey agar is used to distinguish lactose fermenters (pink) from non-lactose fermenters (colourless or pale). It is a selective and differential media. It is selective because bile salts and dyes inhibit gram-positive organisms and gram-negative cocci. It is differential because the pH indicator turns pink-red when the lactose is fermented.

Option D: Chocolate agar is used for gram‐negative intracellular diplococci within phagocytes, Chocolate agar with isovitaleX is the suitable culture medium for Haemophilus ducreyi. H.ducreyi requires the presence of factor X but not factor V and also for Neisseria.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A 40-year-old smoker who is a known case of hypertension was on enalapril and hydrochlorothiazide. He had an episode of hemoptysis and on evaluation he was found to have bronchogenic carcinoma with brain metastasis. His lab values were Na -124 mg/dl, creatinine – 2.8 mg%, blood sugar 112 mg/dl, blood urea - 24 mg/dl, serum osmolality – 255mosm, urine osmolality-350mosm, 24 hour urinary sodium 110 and BP-150/90 mmHg. Which of the following is the most probable diagnosis of the low sodium values in him
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. SIADH

The clinical scenario of patient who is a known hypertensive, smoker and bronchogenic carcinoma with brain metastasis having low sodium, low serum osmolality and high urine osmolality, the most probable diagnosis is of SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate secretion of ADH).

From the given information, reduced serum osmolality rules out pseudohyponatremia(Option D) as such patients should be isotonic or have normal serum osmolality. The BP of the patient indicates there is no hypotension and patient is euvolemic, hence ruling out Cerebral Salt Wasting Syndrome(Option C) in which patient is hypovolemic and volume depleted.  In thiazide induced SIADH(Option B), patients will be dehydrated and not euvolemic.

In this patient, lung cancer and thiazides may cause SIADH.

Bartter and Schwartz diagnostic criteria of SIADH

• Hyponatremia
• Clinically Euvolemic
• Serum osmolality less than 275 mOsm/Kg
• Urine Osmolality more than 100mOsm/Kg
• Urine sodium more than 40 mmol/L
• No use of diuretics

In SIADH, if the hyponatremia is mild and asymptomatic, restrict total water intake to 30 mL/kg/day less than urine output until the syndrome resolves spontaneously. If the hyponatremia is severe and symptomatic, the goal is to partially correct it by intravenous infusion of hypertonic (3%) saline or administration of an AVP antagonist such as tolvaptan or conivaptan. With hypertonic saline or vaptans, plasma osmolarity and sodium should be checked every 1–2 h, and water intake should be adjusted to keep osmolarity 270 mosm/L, at which point the treatment should be discontinued.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is True regarding trematodes?
options: Fasciola hepatica are seen in the intrahepatic biliary radicles
Fasciola hepatica acquired through contaminated water
Triclabendazole is the treatment of choice for all trematode infections
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Fasciola hepatica are seen in the intrahepatic biliary radicles

Of the given statements regarding trematodes, the only true statement is that Fasciola hepatica is seen in the intrahepatic biliary radicles.

Schistosomes are dioecious, Fasciola hepatica is acquired through metacercariae encysted on raw aquatic vegetation and triclabendazole is not the treatment of choice for all trematode infections as praziquantel is used in the management of Schistosomiasis and lung fluke infections.

Trematodes are leaf-shaped unsegmented, flat, and broad helminths. The males are shorter and stouter than the females. The unique feature of flukes is the presence of two muscular cup-shaped suckers (hence called distomata)- the oral sucker surrounding the mouth at the anterior end and the ventral sucker or acetabulum in the middle, ventrally. Three of the most important pathognomic species include Schistosoma hematobium, Fasciola hepatica, and Paragonimus westermani

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.text: Which provision of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) deals with offenses related to medical negligence?
questions.explanation: Section 304 A of the IPC specifically deals with causing death by negligence. It states that "whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide" shall be punished with imprisonment or a fine. In the medical field, this section is applied to cases of criminal medical negligence where a doctor's gross lack of care or rash action results in the patient's death. Section 302 (Option D) is for punishment for murder. Section 304 B (Option B) specifically pertains to "dowry death." Section 301 (Option A) deals with culpable homicide by causing death of a person other than the person whose death was intended. For a doctor to be convicted under 304 A, the prosecution must prove a "gross" degree of negligence that goes beyond mere error of judgment. This section is the primary legal framework for holding medical professionals accountable for fatal negligence
questions.learning: Section 304 — A of the IPC specifically deals with causing death by negligence. It states that "whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide" shall be punished with imprisonment or a fine.

questions.subject: Paediatrics
questions.text: A woman came to OPD with a newborn who has complaints of chest retractions, dyspnea and lethargy. The paediatrician diagnosed the baby with respiratory distress syndrome. This occurs due to the deficiency of:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Lecithin

Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (hyaline membrane disease) is caused by deficiency of pulmonary surfactant, particularly dipalmitoyl phosphatidylcholine (lecithin), produced by type II pneumocytes.

• Lecithin is the major component of surfactant responsible for reducing alveolar surface tension
• Deficiency leads to alveolar collapse (atelectasis), decreased lung compliance, and respiratory distress
• Common in preterm infants due to immature lungs

Clinical relevance:

• L/S ratio (lecithin:sphingomyelin) is used to assess fetal lung maturity
• Antenatal corticosteroids increase surfactant production

questions.text: A patient presents with left-sided head tilt which on straightening leads to right hypotropia. This increases on dextroversion and right head tilt. Paralysis of which of the following muscles is involved?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Right superior rectus

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of right superior rectus palsy.

The Park's-Bielschowsky three-step test is employed to diagnose the muscle paralysis responsible for vertical eye deviation. In this clinical scenario:

1.

Identify the hypotropic eye in primary gaze

•

Right eye is hypotrophic.

•

This could be due to either right eye elevator weakness or left eye depressor weakness.

•

Possible muscles: Right superior rectus, right inferior oblique, left inferior rectus, or left superior oblique

2.

Observe if hypotropia worsens in specific gazes

•

Hypotropia worsens in right gaze (dextroversion).

•

Paralyzed muscle is one that elevates the right eye in right gaze or depresses the left eye in right gaze.

•

Possible muscles: Left superior oblique and right superior rectus.

3.

Determine if hypotropia worsens in head tilts

•

Hypotropia worsens during right head tilt.

•

The right superior rectus is the muscle involved.

Mnemonic for superior oblique paralysis:

• Step 2: Vertical deviation (hypertropia/hypotropia) is Worse On Opposite Gaze – WOOG
• Step 3: Vertical deviation (hypertropia/hypotropia) deviation is Better On Opposite Tilt – BOOT

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A child presents with pinpoint ecchymoses around hair follicles and is not allowing anyone to move his limbs because of pain. He also has tender nodules over the chest, as seen in the image given below. What is the most likely diagnosis in this child?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Scurvy

The given clinical scenario and the image showing scorbutic rosary are suggestive of scurvy.

Scurvy results from the deficiency of vitamin C. Vitamin C is required for the hydroxylation of lysine and proline that are used in the synthesis of collagen. Hence, deficiency of vitamin C leads to the formation of defective collagen.

Defective collagen results in capillary hemorrhages which may present as generalized bleeding tendency. It also results in defective osteoid formation. Subperiosteal hemorrhages cause acute pain and swelling mimicking acute osteomyelitis.

Costo-chondral separation leads to the formation of tender nodules, also known as scorbutic rosary. Rickets also presents with similar nodules at the costochondral junctions known as rachitic rosary. They can be differentiated as scorbutic rosary is more sharply angulated and are painful.
questions.learning: Scurvy — The given clinical scenario and the image showing scorbutic rosary are suggestive of scurvy. Scurvy results from the deficiency of vitamin C.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: Vibration white finger refers to:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Raynaud’s syndrome

Vibration white finger (VWF) is an occupational form of secondary Raynaud’s phenomenon caused by prolonged exposure to hand-transmitted vibration, such as from jackhammers, chain saws, grinders, or pneumatic drills. Repeated vibration causes vasospasm of the digital arteries, leading to episodic finger blanching and ischemia.

Why not the other options?

• A. Buerger’s disease (Thromboangiitis obliterans): An inflammatory occlusive vascular disease affecting young smokers, causing distal ischemia, ulcers, and gangrene rather than vibration-induced vasospasm.
• C. Acrocyanosis: Persistent, painless bluish discoloration of the hands and feet due to vasomotor instability; not episodic and does not show the classic triphasic color change.
• D. Takayasu disease: Large-vessel granulomatous vasculitis involving the aorta and its branches, presenting with absent pulses (“pulseless disease”), not digital vasospasm.
questions.learning: Raynaud’s syndrome Vibration white finger (VWF) is an occupational form of secondary Raynaud’s phenomenon caused by prolonged exposure to hand-transmitted vibration, such as from jackhammers, chain saws, grinders, or pneumatic drills.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.text: A 51-year-old man complains of abdominal pain and blood stained stools. The barium enema study of his intestines shows the following finding. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Intussusception

The given clinical scenario and the radiological image of the claw sign/pincer sign in barium enema is suggestive of intussusception.

Intussusception occurs when a portion of the alimentary tract is telescoped into an adjacent segment. It is the most common cause of intestinal obstruction between 5 months and 3 years of age. The most common location of intussusception is ileocolic.

The combination of paroxysmal abdominal pain, vomiting, and a palpable abdominal mass is a highly characteristic clinical presentation; the presence of associated rectal bleeding invariably confirms the diagnosis. Palpation of the abdomen usually reveals a slightly tender, "sausage-shaped" mass, sometimes ill-defined, which might increase in size during an episode of pain and is most often in the right upper abdomen, with its longitudinal axis cephalocaudal. However, approximately 30% of patients do not have a palpable mass.

Barium contrast enemas demonstrate a filling defect or cupping in the head of the contrast media where its advance is obstructed by the intussusceptum. This is known as the claw sign (shown below). A central linear column of contrast media may be visible in the compressed lumen of the intussusceptum, and a thin rim of contrast may be seen trapped around the invaginating intestine in the folds of mucosa within the intussuscipiens (coiled-spring sign). The intussusception appears as a sausage-shaped mass in a longitudinal plane or a target mass in the transverse plane on CT and USG.

Ultrasound signs include:

* Target sign -also known as the doughnut sign

* Pseudokidney sign: this is seen in the longitudinal section of the bowel:

* The edematous bowel resembles renal parenchyma and

* the mesentery, which is dragged into the intussusception, resembles the renal hilum.

* Crescent in a doughnut sign.

Other options:

Option B: Volvulus presents with constipation, abdominal bloating, nausea and/or vomiting. It shows a coffee bean sign.

Option C: Barium enema radiograph in colonic diverticulitis shows multiple barium-coated outpouchings from the colonic wall and gives the appearance of a saw-tooth. In cases of severe abdominal pain, a CT scan is preferred to avoid the risk of intestinal perforation.

Option D: Ulcerative colitis causes lead pipe appearance.

Pearl PF1800: Barium Studies

Barium swallow: Used to assess the pharynx, esophagus, and stomach. (Barium paste is used)

The image below is a barium swallow showing eosinophilic esophagitis and associated stricture:

Barium meal: Used to assess stomach and duodenum. (95% BaSO4 is used)

Barium meal followthrough: Used to assess the small intestine (50% BaSO4 is used)

Barium enema: Used to assess the large intestine (25% BaSO4 is used)

Pearl PF1850: Radiological findings in various GI disorders

Duodenal atresia: Double bubble sign

Jejunal and ileal atresia: Multiple air-fluid levels (plain erect X-ray abdomen) presenting as triple bubble sign.

Congenital hypertrophic pyloric stenosis: Single enlarged gastric gas bubble - single bubble sign

Sigmoid volvulus: Coffee bean sign

Achalasia cardia: Bird-beak sign
questions.learning: Intussusception — The given clinical scenario and the radiological image of the claw sign/pincer sign in barium enema is suggestive of intussusception. Intussusception occurs when a portion of the alimentary tract is telescoped into an adjacent segment.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.text: What is the minimum amount of fluid to be detected by this X-ray?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 25ml

On a lateral decubitus chest X-ray, as little as \~25 mL of pleural fluid can be detected because fluid layers dependently between the lung and chest wall, making this view the most sensitive plain radiographic method for small pleural effusions.

Minimum pleural fluid detectable:

• Lateral decubitus view: \~25 mL (most sensitive X-ray view)
• PA erect chest X-ray: \~200 mL
• Blunting of costophrenic angle: \~175–200 mL
• Supine X-ray: Often misses small effusions
questions.learning: 25ml On a lateral decubitus chest X-ray, as little as \~25 mL of pleural fluid can be detected because fluid layers dependently between the lung and chest wall, making this view the most sensitive plain radiographic method for small pleural effusions.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.text: Which of the following enzymes is dependent on Vitamin C for its activity?
questions.explanation: Prolyl hydroxylase is a key enzyme in collagen synthesis, responsible for the hydroxylation of proline residues in procollagen. This post-translational modification is essential for the stability of the collagen triple helix. The enzyme requires vitamin C (ascorbic acid) as a cofactor to keep iron (Fe²⁺) in its reduced, active state at the catalytic site. In the absence of vitamin C, prolyl hydroxylase (and lysyl hydroxylase) cannot function effectively, leading to defective collagen formation, which is the biochemical basis of scurvy. Lysyl oxidase (Option B) is also involved in collagen maturation, but it is copper-dependent, not vitamin C–dependent, and is responsible for cross-linking collagen and elastin fibers. Lysyl dehydrogenase (Option A) and hydroxyprolyl kinase (Option D) are not key enzymes in the vitamin C–dependent collagen synthesis pathway. Thus, the enzyme whose activity depends on vitamin C is prolyl hydroxylase, explaining the classic features of vitamin C deficiency such as bleeding gums and impaired wound healing
questions.learning: Prolyl hydroxylase is a key enzyme in collagen synthesis, responsible for the hydroxylation of proline residues in procollagen. This post-translational modification is essential for the stability of the collagen triple helix.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under the Employees’ State Insurance Act, 1948, if the sickness of an insured person is duly certified by an Insurance Medical Officer, periodical cash payment benefit is payable for a maximum period of how many days in any continuous period of 365 days, as Sickness Benefit?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 91 days

The Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) Act, 1948 provides Sickness Benefit as a cash compensation to insured persons who are temporarily unable to work due to certified illness. The benefit is payable at approximately 70% of wages for a maximum of 91 days in two consecutive benefit periods (365 days), provided the insured person fulfills the required contribution conditions.

High-Yield Pearls

• Sickness Benefit: Cash benefit at \~70% of wages. ⭐
• Maximum duration: 91 days in a continuous period of 365 days. ⭐
• Requires certification by an Insurance Medical Officer.
• Available only if the insured person has made the prescribed contributions during the relevant contribution period.
questions.learning: 91 days The Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) Act, 1948 provides Sickness Benefit as a cash compensation to insured persons who are temporarily unable to work due to certified illness.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: What is the vertebral level of the abdominal plane labeled 2?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Upper border of L3

The structure marked '2' in the given image is the subcostal plane. It is at the level of the upper border of the third lumbar vertebra (L3).

The subcostal plane is an anatomical reference plane used in clinical and surgical practice. It is defined as a horizontal plane passing through the lower border of the 10th costal cartilage bilaterally. The 10th costal cartilage corresponds approximately to the level of the upper border of the third lumbar vertebra (L3).

The costal cartilages are extensions of the ribs that articulate with the sternum anteriorly. The 10th costal cartilage is the cartilage of the 10th rib.

In the given image, structure 2 represents the subcostal plane, which corresponds to the level of the lower border of the 10th costal cartilage. Since the 10th costal cartilage is at the level of the upper border of L3, it indicates that the subcostal plane is also at the level of the upper border of L3.

Other options: As mentioned earlier, the subcostal plane is positioned at the level of the upper border of the third lumbar vertebra (L3), not L1 or L2 or L4.

Pearl PF0627: Abdominal planes and their landmarks

Planes that divide the abdomen into 9 regions

* Horizontal planes

* L3 - Subcostal plane (between 10th costal cartilages). Corresponds to the 3rd part of the duodenum

* L5 - Transtubercular plane (between tubercles of iliac crests). Corresponds to the origin of Inferior vena cava.

* Vertical planes (Paramedian or lateral planes)

* Mid-clavicular point to mid-inguinal point on both sides

The nine regions of the abdomen include:

* Left hypochondriac, Epigastric, Right hypochondriac

* Left lumbar, Umbilical (Central), Right lumbar

* Left iliac, Hypogastric (Suprapubic), Right iliac

Other planes and angles in the abdomen

* Transpyloric (Addison's) plane passes midway between the suprasternal notch and the upper border of the pubic symphysis.

* The supracristal plane passing through the highest point of the iliac crest on both sides. Posteriorly, it corresponds to the level of the L4 body or L4/5 disc and its spinous process. It is an important landmark when performing a lumbar puncture or spinal injection. The bifurcation of the abdominal aorta lies approximately in this plane.

* The plane of the pubic crest passes through the upper border of the pubic symphysis. When supine, this plane intersects the tip of the coccyx and the femoral head.

* Renal angle is the angle between the 12th rib and the outer border of Erector spinae muscle. The lower border of normal kidneys may occasionally be felt here.

* Lumbar triangle (of Petit) is marked below by the iliac crest, anteriorly by external oblique and posteriorly by latissimus dorsi. Lumbar herniation can occur here.
questions.learning: Upper border of L3 — The structure marked '2' in the given image is the subcostal plane. It is at the level of the upper border of the third lumbar vertebra (L3).

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A patient comes with palpitation to ER. His Pulse-180/min and BP-70mm of Hg systolic. ECG shows narrow QRS complex tachycardia with regular heart rate. What is the next step in management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. DC Cardioversion

The given clinical scenario of the patient presenting with palpitations and the electrocardiogram (ECG) showing narrow QRS complex tachycardia with regular heart rate suggests a paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia. As the patient is hemodynamically unstable (SBP of 70 mmHg), the next step in management is DC (direct current) cardioversion.

PSVT is a narrow QRS complex tachycardia with sudden onset and termination. It mainly presents with dizziness and palpitations. Evaluation of these patients includes monitoring of vitals and ECG.

The ECG below shows PSVT.

Management of PSVT is as follows:

1) When the patient is hemodynamically stable:

• Carotid sinus massage is attempted. It is avoided if carotid bruit is present and if a prior history of stroke is present
• Valsalva maneuver is done when the patient is cooperative
• Intravenous adenosine is useful in most cases. It is usually given in a bolus dose of 6 mg (IV bolus over 2-3 seconds followed by a rapid flush with 20 mL NS followed by a dose of 12 mg if required. However, its usage is contraindicated in patients with prior cardiac transplantation as it can aggravate bronchospasm and atrial fibrillation.
• Intravenous calcium channel blockers such as verapamil or diltiazem and beta-blockers are helpful but can cause hypotension.
• If there is no termination of the PSVT, then the next step is IV ibutilide + AV nodal–blocking agent (or) IV procainamide + AV nodal–blocking agent (or) cardioversion.

2) When the patient is hemodynamically unstable, i.e. when the patient has hypotension (BP<90/60) with unconsciousness or respiratory distress, QRS-synchronous DC cardioversion is done.
questions.learning: DC Cardioversion — The given clinical scenario of the patient presenting with palpitations and the electrocardiogram (ECG) showing narrow QRS complex tachycardia with regular heart rate suggests a paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the maximum population size observed in relation to reproductive programs?
questions.explanation: The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) is the primary international organization responsible for addressing global population issues and reproductive health. Its mandate includes supporting maternal health, improving access to family planning, and collecting demographic data to help nations manage population growth effectively. While the World Bank (Option A) provides developmental funding, it does not specialize in reproductive programs. UNESCO (Option C) focuses on education, science, and culture. UNICEF (Option D) focuses specifically on child health and development. UNFPA plays a critical role in monitoring population trends to ensure that reproductive health services are scaled to meet the needs of the population size. The organization’s work is central to achieving Sustainable Development Goals related to maternal health and gender equality, ensuring that every pregnancy is wanted and every childbirth is safe. It assists governments in formulating policies that balance demographic shifts with sustainable development goals
questions.learning: The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) is the primary international organization responsible for addressing global population issues and reproductive health.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text:
A woman has vomiting whenever she eats spicy food. Arrange the sequence of events during vomiting.

1. LES is open and UES is closed.
2. Strong contractions in the stomach.
3. Inspiration against a closed glottis.
4. Relaxation of the pyloric sphincter.
5. LES opens and UES opens.
6. Reverse peristalsis in the small intestine.

LES: Lower esophageal sphincter

UES: Upper esophageal sphincter
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 6, 4, 2, 3, 1, 5

The correct sequence of vomiting is 6, 4, 2, 3, 1, 5.

6. Reverse peristalsis in the small intestine.
4. Relaxation of the pyloric sphincter.
2. Strong contractions in the stomach.
3. Inspiration against a closed glottis.
1. LES is open and UES is closed.
5. LES opens and UES opens.

The sensory signals that initiate vomiting are located in the pharynx, esophagus, stomach, and upper portions of the small intestines. Excessive distention or irritation of the duodenum provides a strong stimulus for vomiting. Area postrema constitutes the vomiting centre.

In the early stage, reverse peristalsis begins often minutes before vomiting. It begins far down in the ileum and travels up the intestine. This process pushes a large share of lower small intestine contents to the duodenum and stomach. Relaxation of the pyloric sphincter occurs during this process.

At the onset of vomiting, strong intrinsic contractions are seen in the duodenum and stomach. Once the vomiting centre has been stimulated, inspiration occurs against the closed glottis. It prevents the flow of vomitus into the lungs. The lower esophageal sphincter (LES) is open and the upper esophageal sphincter (UES) is closed at this stage.

The muscles of the abdominal wall contract, building intra-gastric pressure. Finally LES relaxes completely and UES also relaxes allowing the expulsion of the gastric contents.

Note: The esophageal smooth muscle functions as LES at the gastro-esophageal junction. It normally remains tonically constricted. Receptive relaxation of LES occurs when the peristaltic wave passes down the esophagus.
questions.learning: 6, 4, 2, 3, 1, 5 The correct sequence of vomiting is 6, 4, 2, 3, 1, 5. Reverse peristalsis in the small intestine.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.text: A 60-year-old vegetarian presents with fatigue and weakness that have been present for a few months. On physical examination, pallor is noted. Hemoglobin is 9 g/dL and MCV is increased at 110 fL. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Megaloblastic anemia

The most likely diagnosis in this case is megaloblastic anemia, given the patient's vegetarian diet, macrocytosis, and low hemoglobin level.

Megaloblastic anemia can be caused by a deficiency of vitamin B12 or folate. Vegetarians are at increased risk of vitamin B12 deficiency because vitamin B12 is primarily found in animal products. Other conditions can also cause megaloblastic anemia, such as celiac disease, Crohn's disease, and ulcerative colitis. Other causes of high MCV, such as liver disease, alcoholism, and hypothyroidism.

Iron deficiency anemia is characterized by a low hemoglobin level and a microcytic (small cell) anemia. Iron is essential for the production of hemoglobin, and a deficiency of iron can lead to a decrease in hemoglobin levels. However, IDA is typically associated with a low MCV, not a high MCV.

In Aplastic anemia the bone marrow does not produce enough progenitor cells. It can be caused by autoimmune diseases, medications, and radiation. Aplastic anemia can lead to a decrease in all types of blood cells and is associated with a low MCV and a low hemoglobin level, not a high MCV.

Thalassemia is a group of genetic blood disorders that affect the production of hemoglobin. It is characterized by a microcytic anemia. However, thalassemia is not typically associated with a high MCV.
questions.learning: Megaloblastic anemia — The most likely diagnosis in this case is megaloblastic anemia, given the patient's vegetarian diet, macrocytosis, and low hemoglobin level.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: A 22-year-old man presents after an injury with the deformity shown in the image below. This appearance is characteristic of a specific nerve injury. Which nerve is most likely damaged in this condition?
questions.explanation: The image depicts a clinical condition known as "wrist drop," which is the hallmark sign of radial nerve injury. The radial nerve provides motor innervation to the extensor muscles of the wrist and fingers. When this nerve is damaged—often due to a mid-shaft humerus fracture or prolonged pressure in the axilla—the patient loses the ability to extend the wrist against gravity, causing the hand to hang in a flexed position. Injury to the ulnar nerve (Option A) would result in a "claw hand" deformity affecting the 4th and 5th digits. Median nerve damage (Option C) typically leads to the "ape hand" deformity or "hand of benediction" when attempting to make a fist, primarily affecting thumb opposition and finger flexion. Damage to the musculocutaneous nerve (Option D) would result in weak elbow flexion and loss of sensation over the lateral forearm. Therefore, the specific "drop" shown is diagnostic for radial nerve palsy
questions.learning: The image depicts a clinical condition known as "wrist drop," which is the hallmark sign of radial nerve injury. The radial nerve provides motor innervation to the extensor muscles of the wrist and fingers.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A 15-year-old girl presented with a slow-growing, rubbery, non-tender swelling on the side of the neck as shown in the image. Examination shows the presence of freckles and skin patches over the face and trunk. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Neural tumor

A lateral neck mass in a pediatric patient, which is non-tender and present in association with freckles, and hyperpigmented skin patches (cafe-au-lait spots) is suggestive of neural tumor i.e. neurofibroma.

Neurofibroma is a benign tumor arising from the connective tissue of the nerve containing ectodermal, neural and mesodermal connective tissue components. It can be single or multiple. It is the most common intradural extramedullary spinal tumor. Neurofibromas can be local, generalized (von Recklinghausen's disease) or plexiform types. Patients present with mild pain or a painless swelling usually in the subcutaneous or cutaneous plane with tingling, numbness and paraesthesia along the distribution of the nerve. Complications of neurofibroma include cystic degeneration, erosion into deeper planes, cord compression and paralysis (spinal neurofibroma) and sarcomatous changes.

Treatment is excision under general or regional anesthesia. Indications for surgery in neurofibroma include symptomatic patients (pain and pressure symptoms), cosmetic problems and malignant transformation (5%).

Option A: Cystic hygroma is a type of congenital lymphangioma. This swelling is soft and partially compressible, which shows positive fluctuation and translucency test.

Option B: Chemodectoma or carotid body tumor is a rare tumor, most commonly present in the fifth decade and there is an association with pheochromocytoma. These patients usually present with a slowly enlarging, painless lump at the carotid bifurcation.

Option D: A lipoma is a soft painless swelling. It shows the characteristic slip sign and is freely mobile.
questions.learning: Neural tumor — A lateral neck mass in a pediatric patient, which is non-tender and present in association with freckles, and hyperpigmented skin patches (cafe-au-lait spots) is suggestive of neural tumor i.e. neurofibroma.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.text: The image seen below shows_______.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Hysterosalpingography

The image given is of the findings seen in hysterosalpingography. The given image shows bilateral retort-shaped fallopian tubes, indicating bilateral hydrosalpinx.

Hysterosalpingography (HSG) is a technique used for visualization of the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes by the injection of a radioopaque dye, and visualization of the dye by fluoroscopy as it passes through the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes.

It is best performed between the end of the menstrual period and ovulation (i.e. 9th or 10th day of the cycle). 10-15ml of the dye is injected using a Leech-Wilkinson cannula, Rubin's cannula, or Foley's catheter. If the tubes are patent, the dye will spill out of the tubal Ostia and smear the adjacent bowel.

It is used to detect:

• Tubal block: This can be due to strictures (fibrotic block), inspissated amorphous material, or spasms. The tubal spasm can occur in an apprehensive woman, and this is prevented by premedication with atropine and analgesia.
• Uterine anomalies
• Uterine polyps
• Uterine synechiae
• The feasibility of tuboplasty, by studying the location and extent of tubal pathology.

Contradictions:

• Presence of genital tract infection and bleeding
• Genital tuberculosis, due to the risk of spreading infection.
• Suspected pregnancy
• Allergy to the dye
• Premenstrual phase (there is a risk of embolism and endometriosis if HSG is done during this phase).

The image given below shows the appearance of a normal hysterosalpingogram.

Laparoscopic chromopertubation is a laparoscopic procedure for establishing the patency of fallopian tubes or verifying the findings of blocked tubes on HSG. Methylene blue is injected through the cervix to visualize the free spill. The absence of spill indicates blocked tubes.
questions.learning: Hysterosalpingography — The image given is of the findings seen in hysterosalpingography. The given image shows bilateral retort-shaped fallopian tubes, indicating bilateral hydrosalpinx.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A woman with mitral stenosis experiences sudden-onset respiratory difficulty, limb oedema, and abdominal distension. What is the likely clinical diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Pulmonary edema

The likely clinical diagnosis for the woman with mitral stenosis experiencing sudden-onset respiratory difficulty, limb edema, and abdominal distension is pulmonary edema. This is consistent with the pathophysiology of mitral stenosis leading to left atrial hypertension and subsequent pulmonary congestion, resulting in the clinical features described.

Pulmonary edema is the accumulation of fluid in the lung tissue and air spaces. In the context of mitral stenosis, pulmonary edema can occur due to left atrial hypertension and subsequent increased hydrostatic pressure in the pulmonary circulation. This can lead to sudden-onset respiratory difficulty (dyspnea), orthopnea (difficulty breathing while lying flat), paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (sudden awakening with difficulty breathing), limb edema, and possibly coughing up frothy sputum. Therefore, pulmonary edema is the likely clinical diagnosis in this scenario.

Other options:

* Pulmonary embolism occurs when a blood clot (embolus) travels to the lungs, obstructing blood flow in the pulmonary arteries. While pulmonary embolism can cause respiratory difficulty, it typically presents with acute pleuritic chest pain, hemoptysis (coughing up blood), and signs of right heart strain on physical examination. Limb edema and abdominal distension are less commonly associated with pulmonary embolism.

* Cerebral embolism refers to the occlusion of a cerebral artery by an embolus, leading to ischemic stroke. While patients with mitral stenosis are at risk for systemic embolization, presenting as stroke-like symptoms such as focal neurological deficits, sudden-onset respiratory difficulty.

* Paradoxical embolism occurs when a blood clot from the venous circulation crosses into the arterial circulation through a cardiac defect, such as a patent foramen ovale, causing systemic embolization.
questions.learning: Pulmonary edema — The likely clinical diagnosis for the woman with mitral stenosis experiencing sudden-onset respiratory difficulty, limb edema, and abdominal distension is pulmonary edema.

questions.subject: Orthopaedics
questions.text: A man sustains trauma to the lateral aspect of his right knee. Two days later, he develops difficulty in walking due to dragging of the toes and reports numbness over the upper lateral part of the leg and the dorsum of the foot. Which nerve is most likely injured?
questions.explanation: Trauma to the lateral knee, particularly around the fibular neck, often damages the common peroneal nerve because it is superficial and highly vulnerable at that site. Damage here results in "foot drop"—where the toes drag during walking—due to paralysis of the dorsiflexors. It also causes sensory loss over the lateral leg and the dorsum of the foot. The tibial nerve (Option A) controls plantarflexion and sensation on the sole; its injury would not cause foot drop or numbness on the foot's top. The deep peroneal nerve (Option C) is a branch that controls dorsiflexion, but injury to it alone would not explain the sensory loss over the lateral leg. The femoral nerve (Option D) innervates the anterior thigh and is unrelated to foot dorsiflexion. Therefore, the combined motor and sensory deficits specifically identify a common peroneal nerve injury
questions.learning: Trauma to the lateral knee, particularly around the fibular neck, often damages the common peroneal nerve because it is superficial and highly vulnerable at that site.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Open cardiac massage is what kind of wound?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Contaminated

Option B: Contaminated (open cardiac massage)

It is done in emergency situations (not planned, sterile surgery)

• Involves opening chest urgently (often in trauma/arrest) → break in sterile technique→ exposure to contaminants

Clean → planned, no entry into tracts

Clean-contaminated → controlled entry (GI, respiratory, etc.)

Contaminated → trauma, emergency, spillage, breaks in sterility

Dirty → already infected, pus present

questions.subject: Ophthalmology
questions.text: Most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults?
questions.explanation: In adults, Malignant Choroidal Melanoma (often part of uveal melanoma) is definitively the most common primary intraocular malignancy. It typically arises from melanocytes within the choroid and occurs most frequently in middle-aged and elderly individuals. Clinically, it may be asymptomatic or present with blurred vision, floaters, or visual field defects depending on its location. Retinoblastoma (Option A) is the most common intraocular cancer in children, not adults, and is rare after age five. Reticulum cell sarcoma (Option C, now classified as primary intraocular lymphoma) is much rarer and often mimics chronic uveitis. Neurofibroma (Option D) is a benign nerve sheath tumor, not a primary intraocular malignancy. Diagnosis of choroidal melanoma involves dilated fundus examination, ultrasound (showing a characteristic "collar-stud" or "mushroom" shape and low internal reflectivity), and sometimes MRI. Management options include plaque brachytherapy, proton beam radiation, or enucleation in advanced cases. Early detection is critical, as these tumors carry a significant risk of hematogenous metastasis, primarily to the liver
questions.learning: In adults, Malignant Choroidal Melanoma (often part of uveal melanoma) is definitively the most common primary intraocular malignancy. It typically arises from melanocytes within the choroid and occurs most frequently in middle-aged and elderly individuals.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.text: A patient presents to the emergency with epistaxis. There was no relief on pinching the nostrils. Nasal packing was done but the patient still continues to bleed. What would be the next appropriate step in the management of this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Ligation of sphenopalatine artery

The next appropriate step for the management of epistaxis which was not controlled by pinching of nostrils and nasal packing would be ligation of the sphenopalatine artery, as it is the main artery contributing to Kiesselbach’s plexus.

Little's area is the most common site of epistaxis. It is present in the anteroinferior part of the septum. Four arteries anastomose here to form Kiesselbach’s plexus.

The image below shows the blood supply of the nasal septum and areas of epistaxis.

The first step in treating epistaxis is to pinch the nose with the thumb and index finger for about 5 minutes. The patient should sit leaning slightly forward over a basin to spit out blood and breathe through the mouth (Hippocratic or Trotter’s method).

If the bleeding point is localized, cauterization can be done with electrocautery. In cases of uncontrolled bleeding or when the bleeding is posterior into the throat, anterior or posterior nasal packing may be required, respectively. If bleeding continues despite these measures, endoscopic procedures or vessel ligation close to the bleeding point can be considered.

The recommended hierarchy of ligation of vessels in a patient of epistaxis is the sphenopalatine artery first, the internal maxillary artery followed by the external carotid artery, and finally the anterior and posterior ethmoidal arteries.

The sphenopalatine artery is ligated first through a trans-nasal endoscope (transnasal endoscopic sphenopalatine artery ligation) at the sphenopalatine foramen which is situated at the posterior end of the middle turbinate.

However, if the bleeding persists, internal maxillary artery ligation is done at the pterygopalatine fossa via the Caldwell-Luc approach. If bleeding is still not controlled, external carotid artery ligation is done just above the origin of the superior thyroid artery.

If the bleeding site is located superior to the level of the middle turbinate, the anterior and posterior ethmoidal arteries should be ligated via Lynch incision in the medial wall of the orbit.
questions.learning: Ligation of sphenopalatine artery — The next appropriate step for the management of epistaxis which was not controlled by pinching of nostrils and nasal packing would be ligation of the sphenopalatine artery, as it is the main artery contributing to…

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A patient presented to the hospital with a history of increased frequency of micturition. On cystoscopy, a pale ureteric orifice was seen. The patient's KUB X-ray is given below. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Bladder tuberculosis

The given clinical scenario and KUB X-ray point to the diagnosis of bladder tuberculosis.

The earliest sign of tuberculosis of the bladder observed by cystoscopy is the pallor of the mucosa around the ureteric orifice due to submucous edema. Subsequently, tubercles may be seen.

A thimble bladder is a small contracted bladder due to fibrosis of the bladder walls. It is seen in bladder tuberculosis and is appreciated in a micturating cystourethrogram (MCU). The X-ray KUB given above shows a thimble bladder.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In which stage of the demographic cycle is the highest birth rate observed?
questions.explanation: The demographic cycle describes the transition of a population over time as a result of changes in birth and death rates. Stage I (High Stationary stage) is characterized by the highest birth rate (often per 1000), which is counterbalanced by an equally high and fluctuating death rate. This results in a stable or very slowly growing population. In Stage II (Early Expanding, Option B), the birth rate remains high, but the death rate begins to fall significantly, leading to a population explosion. Stage III (Late Expanding, Option C) is marked by a declining birth rate as social and economic conditions improve. Stage IV (Low Stationary, Option D) has both low birth and low death rates. Understanding these stages is vital for national planning and public health policy. Stage I represents the state of many developing nations before the introduction of modern sanitation and medicine. Consequently, the maximum "potential" fertility is typically found in this initial phase
questions.learning: The demographic cycle describes the transition of a population over time as a result of changes in birth and death rates. Stage I (High Stationary stage) is characterized by the highest birth rate (often per 1000), which is counterbalanced by an equally…

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is not an indication of inducing labor?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Placenta previa

Placenta previa is an indication for cesarean delivery, not to induce labor.

Induction of labor is the process of stimulating uterine contractions for vaginal delivery by medical or surgical methods. It is indicated when the benefit to the mother or fetus outweighs the benefit of continuing the pregnancy.

Indications of induction of labor:

*

Gestational hypertension

*

Chronic hypertension

* Pre-eclampsia

*

Post-term pregnancy

*

Abruption placentae

*

IUGR(intra-uterine growth restriction)

*

IUD(Intra-uterine death)

*

Oligohydramnios

Contraindications of induction of labor:

* Contracted pelvis & CPD

* Cord prolapse

* Abnormally implanted placentae

* Previous classical cesarean/ hysterotomy

* Active genital herpes

* Appreciable macrosomia

* Severe hydrocephalus

* Malpresentation

* Pelvic tumor & Ca cervix

* Overdistention or complete transection of the uterus

* Two or more previous low transverse cesarean sections
questions.learning: Placenta previa Placenta previa is an indication for cesarean delivery, not to induce labor. Induction of labor is the process of stimulating uterine contractions for vaginal delivery by medical or surgical methods.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A 5-year-old boy with a known history of asthma presents with sudden breathlessness and wheezing. In the emergency department, his pulse is 140/min, respiratory rate is 28/min, and FEV₁ is 40% of predicted. What is the most appropriate next step in managing this acute asthma exacerbation?
options: A high concentration of oxygen should be given by a face mask + Salbutamol nebulization
High doses of SABA to be given by a nebulizer only
Sedatives should be added to alleviate anxiety
Nebulized anticholinergics to be added immediately as the mainstay of treatment
questions.explanation: The child is experiencing an acute, severe asthma exacerbation, as indicated by tachycardia (140 bpm) and a significantly low FEV1 (40%). The absolute priority in initial management is to ensure adequate oxygenation and provide rapid bronchodilation. Therefore, the combined administration of oxygen via a face mask and nebulized Salbutamol (SABA) is the definitive next step (Option A). SABA alone (Option B) is insufficient if the patient is hypoxic. Sedatives (Option C) are strictly contraindicated in acute asthma because they can suppress the respiratory drive, leading to fatal respiratory failure. While nebulized anticholinergics (Option D) are useful adjuncts in severe cases, they are not the "mainstay" compared to beta-agonists. Therefore, the standard emergency protocol focuses on reversing bronchospasm and preventing hypoxia simultaneously. Rapid intervention is critical to prevent the child from progressing to respiratory exhaustion. Consequently, Option A represents the most comprehensive and life-saving management
questions.learning: The child is experiencing an acute, severe asthma exacerbation, as indicated by tachycardia (140 bpm) and a significantly low FEV1 (40%). The absolute priority in initial management is to ensure adequate oxygenation and provide rapid bronchodilation.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.text: A young boy presented with fissured tongue, lips, and lesions in the angle of the mouth as shown below. On investigation, he had low RBC glutathione reductase activity. Which vitamin is deficient here?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Riboflavin

Clinical presentation of this patient showing cheilosis and stomatitis, combined with low RBC glutathione reductase activity is consistent with riboflavin (vitamin B2) deficiency.

The deficiency state of riboflavin is characterized by the following signs and symptoms:

* Cheilosis: pallor in the angle of mouth and fissuring of lips, which extends radially to skin

* Glossitis: tongue becomes smooth, loss of papilla (magenta-colored tongue)

* Eyes: keratitis, conjunctivitis, corneal vascularisation

* Other features: Seborrheic dermatitis, Anemia

The nutritional status of riboflavin can be assessed by measuring the activity of the RBC glutathione reductase, by FAD added in vitro (this test is specific for riboflavin deficiency).

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Which of the following does not form the inner component of photoreceptors?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Membranous disc

Among the given options, the membranous disc does not form the inner component of photoreceptors but instead forms the outer component.

The other three options i.e., mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, and endoplasmic reticulum form the inner component of photoreceptors.

Photoreceptors (rods and cones) are specialized neurons in the retina with distinct structural components:

• Outer segment: Contains membranous discs that have photopigments (like rhodopsin in rods and photopsins in cones) essential for light detection.

• Inner segment: Contains cellular organelles responsible for metabolism and protein synthesis, such as mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, and endoplasmic reticulum.
questions.learning: Membranous disc Among the given options, the membranous disc does not form the inner component of photoreceptors but instead forms the outer component.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.topic: Hematology · All Qbank Qs Excluding Pyqs
questions.text: A patient presents with recurrent mucosal bleeding and menorrhagia. Lab findings: • Platelets: Normal • PT: Normal • aPTT: Mildly prolonged • Bleeding time: Prolonged Which defect explains these findings?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Defective platelet adhesion

This patient has the classic laboratory profile of von Willebrand disease (vWD), the most common inherited bleeding disorder. von Willebrand factor (vWF) mediates platelet adhesion to exposed subendothelial collagen and also serves as a carrier protein for factor VIII.

• Deficiency or dysfunction of vWF leads to:

• Impaired platelet adhesion → prolonged bleeding time and mucocutaneous bleeding (epistaxis, menorrhagia, gum bleeding).
• Reduced stabilization of factor VIII → mild prolongation of aPTT.

• Platelet count and PT remain normal.

Why not the others?

• B. Defective platelet aggregation → Seen in Glanzmann thrombasthenia (GpIIb/IIIa deficiency), which causes impaired platelet-platelet binding.
• C. Defective fibrin stabilization → Seen in Factor XIII deficiency, characterized by delayed bleeding and poor wound healing.
• D. Defective coagulation factor synthesis → Produces coagulation factor deficiencies with abnormal PT and/or aPTT rather than isolated mucocutaneous bleeding.
questions.learning: Defective platelet adhesion — This patient has the classic laboratory profile of von Willebrand disease (vWD), the most common inherited bleeding disorder. von Willebrand factor (vWF) mediates platelet adhesion to exposed subendothelial collagen and also…

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.text: What is the antidote for belladonna poisoning?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Physostigmine

Belladonna poisoning results from ingestion of plants containing anticholinergic alkaloids such as atropine, hyoscyamine, and scopolamine. These agents competitively block muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, producing the classic anticholinergic syndrome.

Physostigmine is the specific antidote because it is a reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that crosses the blood-brain barrier, thereby reversing both central and peripheral anticholinergic effects.

Why not the other options?

• B. Amitriptyline: A tricyclic antidepressant with anticholinergic properties; it can worsen belladonna poisoning.
• C. Atropine: One of the toxic alkaloids in belladonna; it is not an antidote.
• D. Flumazenil: A benzodiazepine antagonist used for benzodiazepine overdose, with no role in anticholinergic poisoning.
questions.learning: Physostigmine Belladonna poisoning results from ingestion of plants containing anticholinergic alkaloids such as atropine, hyoscyamine, and scopolamine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: A woman in her first trimester of pregnancy is diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and requires anticoagulation therapy. Which anticoagulant is preferred in this situation?
questions.explanation: Managing deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in pregnancy requires an anticoagulant that is effective for the mother and safe for the fetus. Enoxaparin, a Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin (LMWH), is the preferred and standard anticoagulant for use throughout pregnancy. LMWHs do not cross the placenta and therefore carry no risk of fetal teratogenicity or hemorrhage. Warfarin (Option D) is strictly contraindicated in the first trimester as it is highly teratogenic, causing fetal warfarin syndrome (bone and CNS abnormalities). Betrixaban (Option C) is a Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC); currently, DOACs are avoided in pregnancy due to a lack of safety data and evidence that they cross the placenta. Clopidogrel (Option B) is an antiplatelet agent, not an anticoagulant, and is not used for the primary treatment of DVT. Enoxaparin provides a predictable response and generally does not require routine blood monitoring, making it the safest and most reliable choice for gestational anticoagulation
questions.learning: Managing deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in pregnancy requires an anticoagulant that is effective for the mother and safe for the fetus. Enoxaparin, a Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin (LMWH), is the preferred and standard anticoagulant for use throughout pregnancy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A public health researcher is conducting a street-based survey to assess awareness regarding hypertension. To ensure representation, the researcher plans to include a fixed number of participants from each age group and socioeconomic category, based on the known distribution in the city. Interviewers then approach passers-by and recruit participants until the required numbers in each subgroup are reached. No random selection is performed. Which sampling method is being used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Quota sampling

The key features described are:

• Fixed numbers from predefined subgroups (age, socioeconomic status)
• Based on known population distribution
• No random selection within subgroups
• Participants recruited conveniently (street-based) until quotas are filled

This is characteristic of Quota sampling.

Why Quota sampling fits:

• Non-probability sampling method
• Population is divided into subgroups (quotas)
• Interviewers select subjects non-randomly until each quota is met
questions.learning: Quota sampling — The key features described are: • Fixed numbers from predefined subgroups (age, socioeconomic status) • Based on known population distribution • No random selection within subgroups • Participants recruited conveniently (street-based)…

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.text: Which of the following amino acid classifications are correctly matched? 1. Uncharged amino acid – Cysteine 2. Nonpolar amino acid – Proline 3. Basic amino acid – Histidine 4. Basic amino acid – Lysine Choose the correct combination:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1, 2, 3, 4

Amino acids are classified based on the chemical properties of their side chains (R groups) into nonpolar, polar uncharged, acidic, and basic amino acids. Correct classification is fundamental for understanding protein structure and function.

Correct matches:

• 1. Cysteine → Polar uncharged amino acid ✓
• 2. Proline → Nonpolar amino acid ✓
• 3. Histidine → Basic amino acid ✓ (weakly basic; partially protonated at physiological pH)
• 4. Lysine → Basic amino acid ✓

Why are all correct?

• Cysteine contains a sulfhydryl (-SH) group, making it polar but uncharged and capable of forming disulfide bonds.
• Proline is a cyclic nonpolar amino acid that introduces bends in protein chains.
• Histidine contains an imidazole ring and is classified as a basic amino acid.
• Lysine has a positively charged ε-amino group and is a strongly basic amino acid.
questions.learning: 1, 2, 3, 4 Amino acids are classified based on the chemical properties of their side chains (R groups) into nonpolar, polar uncharged, acidic, and basic amino acids.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.text: All of the following statements are true regarding neutrophil extracellular trapping (NET) except that
options: It is detected in blood during sepsis.
It is produced in response to bacterial infection.
It is chromatin with antibacterial enzymes.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Mitochondrial DNA is seen.

Mitochondrial DNA is not seen in neutrophil extracellular traps (NET).

Neutrophilic extracellular traps are networks of extracellular fibers that provide a high concentration of antimicrobial substances at the site of infection and prevent the spread of the microbes by trapping them in the fibrils.

Neutrophilic extracellular traps (NET) are the meshwork of nuclear chromatin of neutrophils. The loss of nuclei leads to the death of the neutrophils. They concentrate antimicrobial peptides and enzymes to fight against bacteria and fungus (not viruses). They are detected in the blood during sepsis. They are produced by neutrophils in response to:

• Infectious pathogens: mainly bacteria and fungi
• Inflammatory mediators: chemokines, cytokines (mainly interferons), complement proteins, and reactive oxygen species (ROS)

Note: The nuclear chromatin in the NETs, which includes histones and associated DNA, has been postulated to be a source of nuclear antigens in systemic autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
questions.learning: Mitochondrial DNA is not seen in neutrophil extracellular traps (NET). Neutrophilic extracellular traps are networks of extracellular fibers that provide a high concentration of antimicrobial substances at the site of infection and prevent the spread of…

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Low apparent volume of distribution of drug indicates
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Not extensively distributed to tissues

Low apparent volume of distribution of a drug indicates that it is not extensively distributed in the tissues.

Apparent Volume of distribution (Vd) = dose administered I.V/ plasma concentration E.g: If a 500 mg of drug A is given i.v (100% bioavailability) and the plasma concentration reached is 10 mg/ liter then the apparent volume of distribution (Vd) is 500/10= 50 liters.

But the normal blood volume is about 5 liters. A high Vd is due to accumulation of drug A in extravascular tissues resulting in low plasma concentration. Therefore, the apparent volume of distribution is an imaginary volume throughout which the drug is distributed if the plasma concentration remains the same throughout.

Option A: t1/2 relationship with volume of distribution (Vd) and clearance (Cl) is given by the formula t 1/2 = 0.693 x Vd /Cl. t1/2 is directly proportional to Vd but it is also inversely proportional to clearance. If a drug has a low volume of distribution but clearance is very low, t1/2 can still be high. So low Vd doesn't always imply low t1/2. So the best answer among the given options is D.

Option B and C: Low Vd does not indicate low bioavailability or low efficacy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The seating arrangement between the doctor and patient is illustrated below. Which of the following statements is correctly describes the risk of transmission of airborne droplet infections in this setting?
options: Setting 1 is better (low risk) for doctor
Setting 2 is better (low risk) for doctor
Setting 1 and Setting 2 both are high risk
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Setting 2 is better (low risk) for doctor

Consultation room layout and airflow direction influence the transmission of airborne and droplet infections. The doctor should sit near the source of fresh air (window), while the patient should sit downstream, so that airflow moves from the doctor toward the patient and then out of the room, minimizing the doctor’s exposure to infectious aerosols.

Why not the other options?

• A. Setting 1 is better (low risk) for doctor: Incorrect; airflow carries respiratory droplets from the patient toward the doctor, increasing exposure.
• B. Setting 1 is better in winters: Incorrect; the principle of airflow direction remains the same irrespective of season.
• D. Setting 1 and Setting 2 both are high risk: Incorrect; Setting 2 reduces the doctor’s risk by optimizing airflow.
questions.learning: Setting 2 is better (low risk) for doctor Consultation room layout and airflow direction influence the transmission of airborne and droplet infections.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Intravenous induction agent of choice for day care anesthesia is____
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Propofol

Intravenous induction agent of choice for day care anesthesia is propofol.

* It has rapid onset of action and a faster recovery.

* It also reduces postoperative nausea and vomiting which provide yet another reason for it to be a preferred drug for outpatient anesthesia.

Note -

* Inhalational agent of choice for day care anesthesia is sevoflurane.

* Muscle relaxant of choice for day care anesthesia is rocuronium.
